JSPrismarine / @jsprismarine/protocol

@jsprismarine/protocol ​

Bedrock packet classes, structures, wire layouts, version gates, and payload builders live here. The package owns protocol encoding; a server supplies game registries and captured data through a ProtocolContext rather than making the protocol package load server data itself.

Supply per-connection data ​

ProtocolContext carries the negotiated protocol version plus the item, block, actor, biome, and jigsaw data that a packet may need. The data stays with the codec that negotiated the connection:

ts
import { ItemRegistryPacket, NetworkBinaryStream } from '@jsprismarine/protocol';
import type { ProtocolContext } from '@jsprismarine/protocol';

const context: ProtocolContext = {
    protocolVersion: 2225
};

const packet = new ItemRegistryPacket();
packet.serialize(new NetworkBinaryStream(), context);
void packet;

The server builds this context from its supported-version captures and current registries. A packet may still receive explicit payload data when the server has generated custom content.

Build payloads from registries ​

The payload subpath translates item, block, creative, and recipe registries into protocol packet payloads. The functions accept those registries as arguments, so the protocol package can encode them without importing a server instance:

ts
import {
    buildBlockProperties,
    buildCraftingData,
    buildCreativeContent,
    buildItemRegistry
} from '@jsprismarine/protocol/payload';

const { properties } = buildBlockProperties([]);
const { entries } = buildItemRegistry([]);
const creative = buildCreativeContent(itemIdsOf(entries), { groups: [], entries: [] });
const crafting = buildCraftingData([]);
void [properties, creative, crafting];

For payload types, NBT helpers, and block palette checks, import from @jsprismarine/protocol/payload. Packet classes and structures are exported from the package root and from their individual module subpaths.

Compression benchmark ​

Run pnpm --filter @jsprismarine/protocol run bench:compression-variants to compare Node's synchronous and asynchronous zlib paths, a resettable zlib stream, and the libdeflate WebAssembly prototype on movement-like and chunk-sized batches. The benchmark checks that each compressed body inflates to the same packet bytes and reports CPU time, throughput, setup cost, allocation notes, and wire size. The WebAssembly package is a development dependency; the server continues to use Node zlib.

AbilityLayerFlag ​

Defined in: minecraft/src/generated/unversioned/AbilityLayerFlag.ts:19

AbilityLayerFlag, from Mojang's published protocol documentation.

Generated - do not edit. Change datagen/manifest.json and run pnpm generate. Source: Mojang/bedrock-protocol-docs@0e00fe80f4f3c71572ff6429de40146d1f4412fc (Minecraft 1.26.40, protocol 2168) Upstream name: AbilitiesIndex

NOT VERSIONED. No bedrock-protocol-docs release describes this enum: a schema exists only for a type some packet field is declared with, and this one travels as a plain integer. The members below come from the last enums.html Mojang published, for Minecraft 1.26.40, and every protocol this package generates reads them unchanged: 2193, 2225.

Treat them as approximate above protocol 2168. A member added since then is missing, and a member removed since then is still here. No source this package will take numbers from publishes this enum per version, so that is a known gap and not something to correct in the generated file.

AbilityLayerType ​

Defined in: protocol/src/packet/UpdateAbilitiesPacket.ts:14

The "SerializedLayer" value of an ability layer, written as a uint16.

The client merges layers in this order, so a flag set in a later layer wins over the same flag in an earlier one. The docs type the field as a bare uint16; the values are the client's AbilitiesLayer enum, CustomCache through LoadingScreen.

AchievementId ​

Defined in: protocol/src/packet/AwardAchievementPacket.ts:14

A MinecraftEventing::AchievementIds member, the game's numbering for its achievements.

The values are the ones the wire carries, from Mojang's enum datagen and the protocol site's 1.26.60-preview.21 changelog. The 1.26.51 type page numbers the members 0 to 81 in list order; that is a rendering artifact, not the wire value. The numbering has gaps where achievements were retired.

CommandArgumentType ​

Defined in: protocol/src/wire/structures/CommandParameter.ts:33

The basic command argument type ids of protocol 2193 (Minecraft 1.26.50).

The numbers are the CommandArgType* constants in gophertunnel's protocol/command.go. They shift between releases, so a parameter is only ever written through CommandParameterType, which ORs them with CommandParameterTypeFlag.Valid.

The ids are a second copy of BedrockParameterTypeId in packages/commands/src/parameterTypes.ts, which is the verified table: it is keyed by the name Mojang's own command metadata spells, and the generator joins the two halves on that key. This package does not depend on @jsprismarine/commands, so the numbers are repeated here and CommandParameter.test.ts reads that file to prove the copies agree. The names below are the common library spelling, which is what the rest of this package reads.

PlayerListAction ​

Defined in: protocol/src/wire/structures/PlayerListEntry.ts:185

The Action byte of a player list entry: 0 adds a player, 1 removes one.

The 1.26.50 docs page lists both values as 0. The client reads Add as 0 and Remove as 1, and the 1.26.60 page corrects the table. The variant selector written before the byte is numbered the other way round: Add selects 1 and Remove selects 0.

ResourcePackStatus ​

Defined in: protocol/src/packet/ResourcePackClientResponsePacket.ts:23

The client's answer in a ResourcePackClientResponsePacket, numbered one above the wire's alternative index so that None can stand for no answer yet.

The docs page is https://mojang.github.io/bedrock-protocol-docs/1.26.51/packets/resource-pack-client-response-packet/ and names the alternatives differently:

  • None has no wire form. Encoding it throws.
  • Refused is Cancel, alternative 0.
  • SendPacks is Downloading, alternative 1, the only one followed by a Downloading Packs list.
  • HaveAllPacks is DownloadingFinished, alternative 2.
  • Completed is ResourcePackStackFinished, alternative 3.

ResourcePackResponse from @jsprismarine/minecraft is the generated equivalent, with the docs names and the same values (CANCEL = 1 through RESOURCE_PACK_STACK_FINISHED = 4). This enum stays exported under its own names because the client package depends on them.

See ​

https://mojang.github.io/bedrock-protocol-docs/1.26.51/packets/resource-pack-client-response-packet/

SubChunkRequestResult ​

Defined in: protocol/src/packet/SubChunkPacket.ts:19

The semantic SubChunkRequestResult values used by the server and clients.

Protocol 2193 writes SUCCESS as 0 and SUCCESS_ALL_AIR as 5. Protocol 2207 shifted the six wire values up by one and reserves 0 for UNDEFINED; the packet codec applies that version difference while keeping this API stable.

LEVEL_CHUNK_DOESNT_EXIST: 2

Defined in: protocol/src/packet/SubChunkPacket.ts:25

The server has no chunk at that column.

PLAYER_DOESNT_EXIST ​

PLAYER_DOESNT_EXIST: 4

Defined in: protocol/src/packet/SubChunkPacket.ts:29

The requesting player is unknown, for example already logged off.

SUCCESS ​

SUCCESS: 1

Defined in: protocol/src/packet/SubChunkPacket.ts:23

Serialized Sub Chunk holds the sub chunk.

SUCCESS_ALL_AIR ​

SUCCESS_ALL_AIR: 6

Defined in: protocol/src/packet/SubChunkPacket.ts:33

The sub chunk is all air, so no Serialized Sub Chunk is needed.

UNDEFINED ​

UNDEFINED: 0

Defined in: protocol/src/packet/SubChunkPacket.ts:21

No result; never sent on purpose.

WRONG_DIMENSION ​

WRONG_DIMENSION: 3

BlockProperty ​

Defined in: protocol/src/packet/StartGamePacket.ts:56

A block the client does not have built in, and the definition it needs to draw it.

Since 1.26.50 this is not only a plugin's blocks: vanilla itself defines some of its blocks in data - the wool stairs and slabs, the concrete slabs - and a real server declares those here too, ninety-odd of them. The definition is carried as bytes rather than modeled: it is network NBT that the server hands on verbatim and the client alone interprets.

Properties ​

definition ​

definition: Buffer

Defined in: protocol/src/packet/StartGamePacket.ts:59

The definition as network NBT (varint string lengths), header byte included.

name ​

name: string

Defined in: protocol/src/packet/StartGamePacket.ts:57

Defined in: protocol/src/packet/ItemStackResponsePacket.ts:23

What a slot holds once the request has been applied.

SubChunkRequestMode ​

Defined in: protocol/src/wire/definitions/levelChunk.ts:28

The sub-chunk count and the optional Client Request SubChunk Limit behind it.

A plain count, then a separate optional limit. The count used to double as a signal: -2 meant the client would ask for sub-chunks itself and was followed by the highest one it could ask for. Since 2168 a count is only a count, and the limit is an optional field of its own, present only in request mode, where the count on the wire is 0 and the payload's count is the limit.

Sub-chunk count in plain mode; the highest requestable sub-chunk in request mode.

Variables ​

ANY_META ​

const ANY_META: 32767 = 32767

Defined in: protocol/src/structure/RecipeIngredient.ts:33

The auxiliary value written for a descriptor that names no single item.

32767 is the wildcard meta, "any", which is what an invalid descriptor and a tag descriptor both stand for. An invalid descriptor writes it in place of a name; a tag descriptor writes it after the tag's name.

CommandParameterType ​

const CommandParameterType: object

Defined in: protocol/src/wire/structures/CommandParameter.ts:92

The type word of a basic command parameter, ready to be written to the wire.

Each entry is a CommandArgumentType id ORed with CommandParameterTypeFlag.Valid, so the two tables cannot disagree. Enum is the bare enum flag; a parameter with an enum attached gets its word built by the packet from the enum's index, not from this value.

DEFAULT_COMPRESSION_LEVEL ​

const DEFAULT_COMPRESSION_LEVEL: 7 = 7

Defined in: protocol/src/CompressionCodec.ts:27

What the server compressed at before the level was configurable.

Higher means less bandwidth and more CPU. Measured on a 10 KiB chunk payload: level 7 costs 0.367 ms, level 1 costs 0.111 ms.

DEFAULT_MAX_DECOMPRESSED_LENGTH ​

const DEFAULT_MAX_DECOMPRESSED_LENGTH: number

Defined in: protocol/src/CompressionCodec.ts:38

Ceiling on what one batch may inflate to.

A compressed payload arrives inside a single RakNet message, so it is bounded by reassembly at roughly 2.8 MiB - but what it expands to is bounded by nothing at all, and both a server and a client here read compressed bytes from a peer they have not authenticated yet. zlib enforces the limit itself rather than us discovering it after allocating.

EMPTY_ITEM_STACK_ID ​

UNCOMPRESSED_BATCH ​

const UNCOMPRESSED_BATCH: 255 = 0xff

Defined in: protocol/src/CompressionCodec.ts:19

"Not compressed", as a batch's prefix byte says it.

The same idea travels at two widths and they do not agree. NetworkSettings negotiates the algorithm in a two byte field, where none is 0xffff; every batch then repeats it in a single byte, where none is 0xff. Reading the byte straight into PacketCompressionAlgorithm therefore matches nothing and throws - which showed up as "Failed to inflate batched content" the moment a client sent its first uncompressed packet, a few packets into a login it had otherwise completed.

byteRotation ​

const byteRotation: WireType<number>

Defined in: protocol/src/wire/definitions/movement.ts:37

An angle as the single byte the movement packets carry it in.

The wire unit is a 256th of a turn, so the conversion is lossy in both directions, and the rounding and the mask are load-bearing: angles accumulate freely either side of [0, 360) and the raw division would hand writeByte a fraction or a number out of range.

FullContainerName: the container name byte, then an optional dynamic id.

Whether the dynamic id travels is decided by the container, not by the protocol version, so the branch lives in this wire type's reader and writer rather than in a gate. levelSoundEventPacket ​

const levelSoundEventPacket: PacketDefinition<{ disableRelativeVolume: WireType<boolean>; entityType: WireType<string>; entityUniqueId: WireType<bigint>; extraData: WireType<number>; fireAtPosition: WireType<Vec3Like | null>; isBabyMob: WireType<boolean>; position: WireType<Vec3Like>; soundName: WireType<string>; }>

Defined in: protocol/src/wire/definitions/levelSoundEvent.ts:72

The LevelSoundEventPacket field list.

Sound Event is the tagged SoundEventIdentifier variant Mojang's 1.26.51 notes describe, either a LevelSoundEvent member or a free sound name. The metadata types it as one string and nothing precedes it: the enum member travels as its name (step, break), so a reader cannot tell the two alternatives apart and does not need to.

The docs page types Fire At Position as a plain Vec3 at 2193 and records the optional from 2207 on. Clients have read a presence byte there since 1.21.70, gophertunnel and PocketMine both write one, and the 2207 entry is the metadata catching up. A bare Vec3 here would hand the client eleven bytes it does not expect.

resourcePackClientResponsePacket ​

const resourcePackClientResponsePacket: PacketDefinition<{ response: WireType<ResourcePackResponseData>; }>

Defined in: protocol/src/wire/definitions/resourcePacks.ts:252

The ResourcePackClientResponsePacket field list: one field, Response.

The schema types Response Type as an int8 and caps Downloading Packs at 65535 entries, which reads like a one byte status and a uint16 count. That is the layout before protocol 2193. Since the Cereal conversion the bytes are the ones above: a 1.26.51 client's DownloadingFinished is 02 13 followed by the 19 bytes of downloadingfinished, and gophertunnel at protocol 2193 writes the same. Until protocol 748 the list was written after every alternative; a real server reads the two stray bytes as the next packet.

scoreboardIdentityInfo ​

const scoreboardIdentityInfo: WireType<ScoreboardIdentityPacketInfo>

Defined in: protocol/src/wire/definitions/scoreboard.ts:201

Scoreboard Identity Info: one entry, with its player id behind a presence byte.

Whether the player id travels is decided per entry by that byte, not by the packet type and not by the protocol version, so the branch lives in this wire type rather than in a gate. Mojang's Cereal conversion note for the packet says the same. Before protocol 2193 the id was written only when the packet type was Update, so a reader keyed on the type is one byte off on every entry.

serverSettingsRequestPacket ​

const serverSettingsRequestPacket: PacketDefinition<{ }>

Defined in: protocol/src/wire/definitions/serverSettings.ts:18

The ServerSettingsRequestPacket field list: empty.

The client asks for the server's settings form while it sets up its settings screen, and the packet arriving at all is the whole message. A server with a form to offer answers with a ServerSettingsResponsePacket; one without answers nothing. The empty list is still a definition so the registry accounts for the packet and the round-trip suite holds it to writing no bytes, which is what a field appearing here by accident would break.

readInventoryAction() ​

readInventoryAction(stream): InventoryActionData

Defined in: protocol/src/wire/structures/InventoryTransaction.ts:187

Reads one action.

The Container ID and the Bit Flags are each an optional with its own presence byte. Up to protocol 748 the reader inferred their presence from the Source Type. The client still sets each byte by that rule (a container has a Container ID, the world has Bit Flags), but the byte is what is on the wire, and a reader that infers instead of reading is one field off as soon as the two disagree.

Parameters ​

stream ​

BinaryStream

The stream positioned at the Source Type.

InventoryActionData

The action's six fields.

readItemStackRequest() ​

readItemStackRequest(stream, protocolVersion?): ItemStackRequest

Defined in: protocol/src/wire/structures/ItemStackRequest.ts:333

Reads one ItemStackRequest: Client Request Id, Actions, Strings To Filter, StringsToFilterOrigin.

Each action opens with two numbers that mean the same thing: a varuint variant index, which is the action's position in the oneOf list, and then the Action type as a byte. The variant index is what is dispatched on. Protocol 2225 inserts CraftReservedAction at type 18, shifting the two deprecated craft actions; the selected layout follows the supplied protocol version. The echoed Action type byte is read and dropped.

Parameters ​

stream ​

BinaryStream

The stream positioned at Client Request Id.

protocolVersion? ​

number = protocolVersion2193

The negotiated protocol version; defaults to 2193.

Returns ​

ItemStackRequest

Throws ​

when the action count is above MAX_REQUEST_ACTIONS, or an action or descriptor type is unknown.

readPacketId() ​

readPacketId(buffer): number

Defined in: protocol/src/NetworkPacket.ts:17

Reads the packet id from a Bedrock packet header without consuming its body.

The header is an unsigned varint. Its low ten bits are the packet id; sender and target subclient ids occupy the bits above them. For a truncated varint, the bytes that are present still contribute to the returned id; callers can pass it through their ordinary packet lookup.

Parameters ​

buffer ​

Uint8Array

Encoded packet bytes positioned at the header.

Returns ​

number

The packet id in the low ten bits of the header.
